newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel would keep Thomson-CSF listed.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel would keep Thomson-CSF listed.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk said on Friday in an interview with Le Monde that he wanted to have a substantial stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF which would remain a listed company.
Tchuruk urged the government to decide to sell its 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF through a private placement and not via a public sale.
The government is expected to announce its decision on the sale of its stake in Thomson-CSF before the end of February after it had to suspend a previous privatisation attempt in December.

He said an alliance of Alcatel, Thomson-CSF, Dassault Aviation and Aerospatiale would form a strong French group capable of leading negotiations with other major European defence groups such as GEC Plc and Daimler-Benz Aerospace.
"I do not close the door to (smaller French groups) Sagem or Cie des Signaux. But first we have to restructure the industry around those that have an important size," he told Le Monde.
He said the plan had four main elements. In the defence electroncs field, Dassault would bring its Dassault Electronique unit into Thomson-CSF.
"We would finally be able to celebrate the wedding that has so many times been postponed," he said.
In military telecommunications, Tchuruk said an alliance of Thomson-CSF and Alcatel would create the world leader in the sector.
He said that in satellites, there was the Matra Marconi Space joint-venture of Lagardere and GEC Plc, French companies Alcatel and Aerospatiale and DASA of Germany.
"In this sector, there is enough (business) to keep two big players, at least in Europe," he said, adding there were strong synergies between Alcatel and Aerospatiale.
Fourthly, in missiles there is Matra British Aerospace, DASA, Aerospatiale and Thomson-CSF.
"We believe that in a first stage it will be possible to keep two players. There will maybe later be a convergence but let's not go too quickly," he said.
He said that the stake of Alcatel in Thomson-CSF had to be "substantial" and "strong" but he had no plans to absorb the company into Alcatel, as in a previous attempt to obtain the group.

"This time we keep the group intact. It will keep its management team, it will have a number of big shareholders, it will remain listed on the Bourse and there will be place for staff-shareholders. Alcatel will be the biggest shareholder," Tchuruk said.
He said that the alliance of Alcatel, Aerospatiale, Dassault and Thomson-CSF would create a strong group capable of negotiating on a world scale.
"We will be in a position to start, in a second stage, European alliances with for instance GEC or DASA," he said, adding that there were currently no negotiations with any foreign company.
The other declared candidate for buying the state's stake in Thomson-CSF is Lagardere Groupe, owner of Matra Defence Espace.
